title: Redshifted Cool Gas in the Disturbed HI Disk of the Starburst Dwarf NGC 4214
summary: We report redshifted cool gas toward the central star-forming region of the nearby starburst dwarf galaxy NGC 4214. HST/COS spectra show low-ionization absorbers redshifted relative to the systemic velocity, most clearly in SII ($Δv=19.8\pm2.6\ {\rm km\,s^{-1}}$) and supported by MgII ($Δv=30.3\pm3.0\ {\rm km\,s^{-1}}$), while PII remains tentative ($Δv=7.5\pm3.4\ {\rm km\,s^{-1}}$). The Keck/HIRES spectra also reveal a redshifted CaII absorption component ($Δv=25.6\pm1.5\ {\rm km\,s^{-1}}$). Because the absorption is detected against the central UV or optical continuum, the gas must lie in the foreground of the star-forming region and is moving away from the observer and toward the background UV source in projection. A VLA--THINGS HI spectrum extracted at the COS position within one VLA beam also shows a redshifted neutral component at $v_{\rm hel}=329.2\pm0.9\ {\rm km\ s^{-1}}$, offset by $38.2\pm1.3\ {\rm km\ s^{-1}}$ from systemic and by $27.6\pm1.0\ {\rm km\ s^{-1}}$ from the dominant local HI component. The FAST HI mapping further reveals an extended, kinematically disturbed neutral disk, with residual structures relative to a warped-disk model. Together, the redshifted UV absorption, the redshifted HI component, and the disturbed large-scale HI velocity field show that the central anomalous cool gas is observed in a galaxy with a disturbed extended neutral disk. This geometry suggests that the redshifted cool gas may trace inflow or recycled fallback toward the central region, although warped-disk or non-circular disk motions cannot be fully excluded.

title: OGLE-2016-BLG-0523: A Low-mass Brown Dwarf or super-Jupiter in a $>100$ au Orbit
summary: To search for very wide-orbit binary-lens events, we cross-match microlensing events detected by OGLE-IV and KMTNet between 2011 and 2024. After removing contaminants from variable stars, we identify OGLE-2016-BLG-0523 as a microlensing event showing two short-lived bumps in its light curve, with the two separated by 8.36 yr. We investigate three scenarios to explain the two bumps, including a binary-lens single-source (2L1S), a single-lens binary-source (1L2S), and two unrelated single-lens single-source events (2$\times$1L1S). The 1L2S interpretation is excluded due to its poorer fit to the data, while the 2$\times$1L1S scenario is disfavored by the low event rate, unphysical total source flux, and unphysical color for one of the two putative sources. For the surviving 2L1S interpretation, the Einstein timescales of the two bumps are $8.343 \pm 0.076$ days and $3.231 \pm 0.047$ days, respectively, implying a binary mass ratio of $q = 0.15$. A Bayesian analysis indicates that the primary lens is most likely a low-mass M dwarf, while the companion is probably a low-mass brown dwarf or super-Jupiter. The inferred projected separation is about 450 au, making the companion the widest low-mass object discovered via microlensing to date. Our discovery highlights both the promise and challenges of identifying very wide, low-mass companions through microlensing. Although upcoming facilities such as Roman and Earth 2.0 space telescopes will improve sensitivity to such events, overcoming degeneracies and distinguishing them from variable phenomena will remain essential for building a robust statistical sample.

title: A Relationship Between Fast Radio Burst Dispersion Measure and Host Galaxy Inclination
summary: It is commonly thought that fast radio bursts (FRBs) trace star formation, and that they are produced by magnetars. Both hypotheses imply that their sources are hosted primarily (but not exclusively) in galactic disks. Although there is evidence in that direction, it has yet to be shown conclusively. In addition, a tension exists with the fact that at least one FRB source is found in a globular cluster far from the disk of the host. If FRBs originate primarily in disks, the galaxy orientation could leave an impression in the sample of observed FRBs, either as a selection bias against FRBs in edge-on galaxies or as a correlation with DMHost. Statistical tests against the inclinations of FRB host galaxies, derived from parametric morphology applied to optical and near-infrared imaging, can search for these effects. Such a search requires an adequately large sample of known FRB hosts that have been imaged to a sufficient depth, while estimates of DMHost also require the redshift of each host to be known. These conditions are best met in the Commensal Real-time ASKAP Fast Transient (CRAFT) survey sample of FRB host galaxies, for which the majority have been imaged at optical wavelengths with FORS2 on the Very Large Telescope (VLT). Here these data are fitted with the morphology software GALFIT to derive the elliptical axis ratio q (a proxy for inclination) for 34 hosts from the CRAFT sample, detected with ASKAP and followed up with VLT imaging. We find no bias against FRB detections from edge-on galaxies; instead, we uncover a new relationship between the inclination of an FRB host galaxy and DMHost. This is consistent with a primarily disk-based origin for CRAFT FRBs. Using this relationship we are able to reduce the scatter of the host sample about the Macquart relation by 40%, demonstrating a new empirical method for estimating DMHost that requires only deep optical imaging.

title: Direct detection constraints on EFT operators for inelastic dark matter
summary: We convert existing exclusion limits on the elastic spin-independent (SI) dark matter--proton cross sections into upper bounds on the event rate, subsequently applying them to constrain other effective operators for inelastic scattering of light dark matter in the GeV mass region. We focus on three representative scenarios including the isoscalar, proton-philic, and the proton-philic spin-dependent inelastic dark matter model, which are well-motivated in phenomenological studies of dark matter detection.

title: ASKAP Monitoring of the Rubin Deep Drilling Fields
summary: In the past decade, time domain astronomy surveys across the multi-messenger spectrum have developed "alert streams" which circulate observational information in real-time to the wider astronomical community. Despite this being standard practice for optical, gamma-ray and gravitational wave time domain astronomy for several years now, this kind of infrastructure has not yet been deployed at-scale for radio telescopes. We are conducting a long-term monitoring program that targets the Rubin Deep Drilling Fields using the Australian SKA Pathfinder (ASKAP). The primary goal of this program is to provide serendipitous radio observations of all objects of interest in these fields, and circulate that information in as close to real-time as possible. In this manuscript we outline the survey plans and status, the infrastructure we have developed to disseminate this information and an initial data release comprising 5 months of ASKAP observations of each field (although only 3 months overlaps with Rubin) conducted on an approximately 10 day cadence with a noise level of $\sim 60\,μ$Jy. As part of this data release, we present updated high-cadence radio light curves to the tidal disruption event AT2018hyz and the supernova SN2024abfo along with the discovery of two new radio variables, a possible tidal disruption event ASKAP J095711.5+051205 and an in-progress extreme scattering event ASKAP J005026.4-422958. The scientific results from this program along with the infrastructure developed to acquire them will lay the foundation for the integration of future radio imaging surveys into the broader multi-messenger alert stream, leading the way for major facilities such as the Schmidt Observatory System and the SKA.

title: Global analysis of tensor mode helicity
summary: A detection of helicity in a primordial gravitational-wave background (GWB) would provide compelling evidence for parity violation in the early universe and point toward physics beyond the standard picture of inflation. Since big bang cosmology is not time translation invariant, we identify that the so-called ``regular'' and often-neglected ``irregular'' solutions are independent degrees of freedom that can in principle carry different, even opposite, helicities. We note that this possibility complicates the interpretation of a measured net helicity. To determine the sensitivity of various GW detector configurations to helicity, we introduce a universal helicity efficiency coefficient that provides a unified geometric description of helicity sensitivity across gravitational-wave detectors which generalizes and improves previous estimators. We apply this helicity efficiency coefficient to estimate the sensitivity of a range of future GW experiments to helicity across twenty orders of magnitude in frequency assuming a fully helical background with an amplitude just below the current constraints.

title: Decomposing the Kinematics of SNR G180.0-01.7 with Medium-Resolution Spectra
summary: The exceptionally large angular diameter and intrinsic optical faintness of the Galactic supernova remnant (SNR) G180.0-01.7 (S147) have historically hindered a comprehensive spectroscopic census of its filamentary structure. We present the first dedicated medium-resolution (R ~ 7500) spectroscopic study of S147 using the LAMOST Medium-Resolution Spectroscopic survey of Galactic Nebulae (MRS-N). By implementing multi-Gaussian decomposition on the H$α$, [NII], and [SII] emission complexes and applying combined spectroscopic and spatial criteria, we disentangle the shock-ionized filaments of the SNR from the pervasive foreground and background Diffuse Ionized Gas (DIG). Our analysis reveals a distinct bimodal radial velocity distribution for the SNR: a low-velocity population tracing the decelerated forward shock at a dense cavity wall, and a high-velocity population (with absolute radial velocities of ~ 70 $\pm$ 30 km/s) corresponding to ejecta within a low-density cavity. The co-existence of these populations provides kinematic evidence for the "supernova-in-a-cavity" scenario. Furthermore, we detect enhanced [SII]/H$α$ ratios in the DIG along the eastern and northern boundaries of the remnant, signaling shock compression of the ambient interstellar medium and highlighting remnant's multifaceted feedback.

title: Phantom Zernike Wavefront Sensor: Phase Contrast with Engineered Focal Plane Reference Speckles
summary: We introduce the Phantom Zernike Wavefront Sensor (phantom ZWFS), an engineered reference extension of phase-contrast wavefront sensing in which controlled pupil plane modulation generates off-axis coherent speckle structures that undergo localized focal plane phase shifts. These references may replace the central ZWFS reference when the on-axis PSF core is required for another optical function, such as photonic science coupling, or may augment a conventional central ZWFS response to provide additional wavefront information. Using a monochromatic scalar model, we derive the resulting carrier structure and show how the engineered references can be recovered through spatial demodulation and incorporated into calibrated reconstruction. A simple four-reference realization demonstrates that the reference geometry redistributes photon sensitivity across spatial frequency magnitude and orientation, producing mode dependent changes in linearity and cross-talk rather than a uniform improvement over a classical ZWFS. We then consider differential piston on a seven segment aperture as an application specific example. A hybrid sensor retaining the central ZWFS phase region and adding six engineered references that match the segment geometry gives similar precision near the phased state but substantially improved performance at larger piston excursions. Under the adopted photon-noise-limited benchmark, the hybrid reduces the nonlinear reconstruction error and provides better conditioned optical encoding of the piston state than an idealized vector ZWFS, allowing more precise piston estimation from the same detected photon flux at larger piston excursions.

title: Combination of multi-observatory photometry to determine asteroid rotation periods
summary: This study aims to determine asteroid rotation periods from sparse, unevenly sampled, multi-observatory photometry using the Lomb-Scargle (L-S) method. The photometric measurements of the asteroids are taken from the circulars of the Minor Planet Center (MPC). Twelve asteroids, four of them with known rotation periods, were analyzed with two complementary methods. In the separate dataset analysis (S-method), each observatory dataset was analyzed separately, and the final period was obtained as a weighted average of the consistent candidate periods, with weights based on the peak power of the power spectrum, the number of measurements, and the quality of the corresponding light curve fit. In the combined dataset analysis (C-method), all measurements were corrected for the biases of the photometric band, the star catalog and the observatory, reduced to a common scale and merged into a single dataset, after which the period was derived directly from the L-S analysis of the combined time series. Both methods produced consistent results, and they reproduced the known periods of the four test asteroids within 0.05%. The results show that the L-S method is well suited for finding rotation periods in sparse observations with uneven sampling over long time intervals. New rotation periods were found for asteroids 2968, 2971, 3081, 3473, 3716, and 4303. The period of 2968 remains ambiguous because of daily aliasing. For 3716, the most likely period is 10.474 hours, but its daily alias at 13.405 hours cannot be excluded completely. For 3173, the strongest peaks at 22.99 and 45.98 hours are probably daily aliases of a slower brightness variation. For asteroid 2607, the period agrees with a recently published value and is more precise. The approach is therefore promising for automated searches for unknown asteroid rotation periods.

title: The Population of Type~1 Active Galactic Nuclei in Dark Energy Spectroscopic Instrument. I. Profile-dependent Measurements of the Low-redshift Sample
summary: We present a spectral analysis of a large sample of low-redshift type 1 active galactic nuclei (AGNs) selected from the first data release of the Dark Energy Spectroscopic Instrument (DESI DR1). For objects at $z\le0.9$, we perform spectral fitting and ML-assisted refinement, yielding 114,754 type 1 AGNs. We use two fitting schemes that differ only in the broad-line model: the broad Balmer components are fitted with either a Lorentzian function or a sum of Gaussians. The continuum and [O III] luminosity measurements agree closely between the two schemes, whereas the Gaussians scheme generally yields larger broad-H$β$ full width at half maximum (FWHM) values, larger virial black hole masses, and lower accretion rates. The adopted broad-Balmer profile also changes the decomposition of narrow Balmer emission. Specifically, the anti-correlation between [O III]$\lambda5007$/narrow H$β$ and accretion rate is stronger under the Gaussians scheme with a Spearman rank correlation coefficient $r_{\rm s}=-0.412$, than under the Lorentzian scheme with $r_{\rm s}=-0.206$; the same tendency is observed in the narrow-line Seyfert 1 galaxies (NLS1s) subset ($r_{\rm s}=-0.435$ and $-0.259$ for the Gaussians and Lorentzian schemes, respectively), suggesting that the Gaussians scheme may provide a more self-consistent separation of the broad and narrow H$β$ components. Moreover, the consistent correlations recovered under both profile prescriptions favor a continuous type 1 accretion-state sequence, with NLS1s occupying its high-accretion end rather than constituting a distinct population.

title: Simulation Study of Reconstruction of Cosmic Ray Extensive Air Shower with Thermal Neutron Detected by ENDA
summary: In the investigation of the "knee" region within the cosmic ray energy spectrum, extensive air shower (EAS) reconstruction by using different EAS secondary particles are of paramount importance for energy determination and composition separation and finally measurement of energy spectrum of different cosmic ray composition. The Electron-Neutron Detector Array (ENDA) is designed to detect thermal neutrons generated in the ground by high energy hadrons which constitute the "backbone" of EAS and carry vital information regarding the primary cosmic rays. At present, ENDA-64, consisting of 64 detectors, is employed inside the Large High Altitude Air Shower Observatory (LHAASO). This work simulates the response of ENDA and investigates the lateral distributions of thermal neutrons. A comparison of the NKG and double-exponential functions for describing this distribution using MC simulation data shows that the double-exponential function is more accurate. The mean difference between fitted and measured thermal neutron density is within ~ 6%. Meanwhile, the thermal neutron density at 10 m from the shower axis, $ρ_n$, depends mainly on the sum of all hadrons energy or the number of high-energy hadrons. The relationship between $ρ_n$ and EAS hadron energy or the number of high-energy hadrons can be well fitted by a linear function on a log scale. This work is fundamental for energy determination and composition separation with hybrid detection by using ENDA in the near future.

title: Stochastic gravitational waves from narrow-band cosmological magnetic fields
summary: We calculate the spectrum of gravitational waves generated by a cosmological magnetic field with a narrow-band power spectrum. For a spectrum narrowly peaked at a comoving wavenumber $k_c$, we find that the gravitational wave signal peaks at $2k_c$ and has a sharp cutoff at this scale. We apply this result to an ultralight dark matter model of magnetogenesis operating around recombination, in which an axion-photon coupling generates a helical magnetic field by parametric resonance. We determine the conditions for the resulting gravitational waves to enter the frequency range of pulsar timing experiments. Although the required frequency can be reached for sufficiently large coupling, the corresponding amplitude is below the experimental sensitivity for physically allowed energy densities of the magnetic field. We generalize this conclusion to models of magnetogenesis operating at other epochs, estimating as $T \simeq 160 \mathrm{MeV}$ the temperature of a magnetogenesis process assumed to be the source of the stochastic gravitational wave background suggested by pulsar timing arrays. We place the lower bound $T \gtrsim 1$-$10 \mathrm{MeV}$ on such viable models.

title: The Fast & Fourier: Using neural operators to speed up radiative modeling of protoplanetary disks
summary: Edge-on protoplanetary disks provide a spatially resolved view of the vertical distribution of icy planetary building blocks, but inferring their relative abundances requires radiative-transfer (RT) modeling with multiple anisotropic scattering. Each model costs $10^{1}$-$10^{3}$ CPU hours, which precludes principled Bayesian inference and homogeneous, population-scale analyses. We develop and validate a fast and reusable surrogate for Bayesian inference with ice-bearing edge-on disk models. We train a Fourier Neural Operator on a grid of RADMC-3D spectra. The network maps disk parameters and analytic physical input fields to the spectrum, using mixed-resolution spectra. We use the surrogate in an explicit-likelihood nested sampler and validate it on held-out simulations and synthetic recovery tests with TARP coverage. Finally, we use it to retrieve the disk structure and ice abundances of ESO-H$α$ 569 from its spectral energy distribution. The surrogate reproduces the RADMC-3D spectra with a median error of 4.84%. We recover synthetic parameters without detectable bias and with nominal coverage. For ESO-H$α$ 569, the posterior favors a massive ($M_{\rm gas}=0.028^{+0.015}_{-0.011}\,M_\odot$), nearly edge-on ($i=79.8^{+5.2}_{-2.4}$ deg) disk consistent with the image-plus-SED model of Wolff et al. (2017). Its ice abundances and cavity size remain weakly constrained by broadband data alone. The marginal spectrum-evaluation speed-up is $\sim10^{9}$-$10^{10}$. Neural-operator emulation makes full posterior inference feasible within the adopted model and training prior. Key posterior points should still be checked with high-fidelity RT models. By drastically cutting evaluation time, this approach enables for the first time homogeneous population studies of ices in disks, which new JWST surveys can capitalize on to map the range of compositions within planetary nurseries.

title: X-Shooter view of planetary nebulae microstructures I: The case of NGC 7009 knots
summary: The properties of NGC 7009 knots are investigated by employing UV-to-near-infrared data from the X-Shooter spectrograph. These structures belong to the category of low-ionization structures (LISs), which are characterized by enhanced emission from low-ionization species and whose origin remains enigmatic. Our main goal is to conduct the first dedicated spectroscopic study of LISs using X-Shooter, that covers a wide spectral range from the UV to the near-IR, simultaneously. As a pilot study, we focus on NGC 7009 to investigate its ionized, atomic, and molecular gas, aiming to better characterize the physical properties of its LISs and explore their largely unexplored molecular content. The spectrum was processed through the ESO Reflex pipeline, and the physical properties of LISs were derived with the latest version of PyNeb. More than 250 emission lines were detected in the spectra of NGC 7009 LISs, including rare, forbidden transitions from low- ionization species such as Fe+ and Ni+, as well as two transitions from P+, identified here for the first time in LISs. The detection of multiple shock tracers, together with the shock excitation of [Fe II] and [O I], as revealed by emission-line diagnostics, supports the presence of shocks at LISs. The richness of the spectrum allowed us to derive electron temperatures and densities at the LISs using both collisionally excited and optical recombination lines. In the near-IR spectrum of the LISs, nine ro-vibrational H2 emission lines were detected, seven of which were reported here for the first time. These lines were used to construct the H2 excitation diagram, providing new insights into the physical conditions of the nebular gas. The excitation of molecular hydrogen is most likely dominated by collisional processes through shocks.

title: In-flight Timing Calibration of the Follow-up X-Ray Telescope on Board the Einstein Probe
summary: After the launch of Einstein Probe (EP), pulsars are observed to calibrate the timing system of the onboard Follow-up X-ray Telescope (FXT) by measuring the times of arrival (TOAs). FXT has two independently operating modules, namely FXTA and FXTB, each equipped with the Wolter-I optics and the pnCCD camera. For scientific observations, each pnCCD has three distinct readout modes that differ in frame cycles, the full frame mode (FF, 50 ms per frame), the partial windowed mode (PW, 2.2 ms per frame), and the timing mode (TM, 23.68 $μ$s per row, 9.4352 ms per frame). Thus, 1RXS J170849.0--400910 with the spin period of 11 s is observed in FF, PSR B1509--58 (150 ms) in PW, and Crab pulsar (33 ms) in TM as well as PSR B1821--24 (3.05 ms) and PSR B1937+21 (1.56 ms). The TOAs of these pulsars measured by FXTA and FXTB are compared with the results of NICER, and for Crab pulsar with the Jodrell Bank Monthly Ephemeris (JBE). Results verify that the timing system of FXTA and FXTB in FF, PW, and TM modes are consistent with each other, and are in good alignment with NICER. The measured advance of the Crab pulsar's main peak relative to JBE is $357^{\pm14(stat)}_{\pm54(sys)} μ$s in FXTA and $394^{\pm14(stat)}_{\pm67(sys)} μ$s in FXTB. Based on measurements of PSR B1821--24 and PSR B1937+21, the preliminary absolute timing accuracy is estimated to be 6 $μ$s for FXTA and 31 $μ$s for FXTB in TM mode. Additionally, the systematic delay of FXTA timing results relative to FXTB is found to be $20^{\pm19(stat)}_{\pm21(sys)} μ$s.

title: When dust growth takes over: the origin of dust in post-reionization galaxies
summary: The post-reionization epoch ($z\sim4$-6) marks a critical phase in galaxy evolution, during which galaxies rapidly assemble their stellar mass, enrich their interstellar medium, and build up substantial dust reservoirs. The physical processes responsible for such rapid dust enrichment remain uncertain. We investigate the dust enrichment history of the ALPINE-CRISTAL-JWST (ACJ) sample using the semi-analytic galaxy formation model GAlaxy Evolution and Assembly (GAEA), which follows galaxy assembly, chemical enrichment, and dust evolution. We select model galaxies matching the observed stellar masses, star formation rates, and metallicities of the ACJ sample, compare their dust properties with observed scaling relations, and trace their enrichment histories and environments. The model reproduces the observed dust mass-stellar mass relation and the dust-to-stellar mass, dust-to-gas, and dust-to-metal ratios as functions of stellar mass and metallicity. Reproducing these constraints requires efficient dust growth in the interstellar medium; stellar dust production alone cannot account for the observed dust reservoirs, even under the most optimistic assumptions. The combination of stellar mass, star formation rate, and metallicity provides a good predictor of galaxy dust content. Our model suggests rapid dust build-up consistent with the previously noted rapid metal enrichment, with evidence for a transition around $z\sim8$-9 below which dust growth becomes the dominant dust formation channel. Finally, ACJ-like galaxies preferentially reside in locally overdense environments, suggesting that environment may have contributed to their accelerated evolution. Taken together, these results support rapid and coupled stellar, metal, and dust build-up in ACJ galaxies during the post-reionization era.

title: The road to $H_0$, $Ω_m$, and $w$ with a global neutrino-telescope network
summary: The newly measured correlation between the neutrino and X-ray luminosities of Seyfert galaxies has yielded the first neutrino-based measurement of the Hubble constant. Building on this result, we forecast the reach of a global neutrino-telescope network by 2030, utilizing full-sky IceCube exposures combined with KM3NeT-ARCA and Baikal-GVD. We find that this 2030 configuration sharpens the neutrino-measured Hubble constant from today's $H_0 = 66^{+44}_{-37}$ to $H_0 =66^{+15}_{-13}$ km s$^{-1}$ Mpc$^{-1}$. Additionally, we project that the disk-corona slope of the neutrino X-ray luminosity relation ($L_ν\propto L_X^β$) will reach $β=0.72\pm0.04$, enabling a $\geq \!5σ$ exclusion of the calorimetric value $β=1$. Finally, we show that, if a high-redshift population of neutrino sources, such as JWST's "little red dots," is identified and obeys the same luminosity relation, we can obtain a new independent measurement of the matter density $Ω_m$ and the dark energy equation-of-state parameter $w$.

title: Seeing in the Dark: Gravitational Waves from Resonant Production of Dark Photon Dark Matter
summary: Ultralight dark photons (DPs) are well-motivated dark matter candidates. A promising yet underexplored mechanism for their relic abundance is parametric resonance in the Abelian-Higgs model that generates the DP mass. We advance previous analytical studies through dedicated 3D lattice simulations that capture important nonlinear effects, including backreaction and relic partitioning between the dark Higgs and DPs. We further predict the associated stochastic gravitational-wave (GW) signal, which can be within reach of a broad range of detectors, opening a new avenue to probe ultralight DP dark matter.

title: A Burst of Reionization in the Dark Ages
summary: Primordial overdensities at small scales can be significantly larger than those observed at large scales. As a result, they can collapse much earlier, at redshifts $z \sim 100$. In these collapsed halos, stars and black holes can form, where they can then contribute to an early reionization of the universe. If this epoch is temporary, the free electrons will recombine yielding a low level of ionization leading into cosmic dawn. This contributes to the optical depth of the universe, and adds more weakly to low-$\ell$ polarization signals of ionization compared to later sources. We study the effects of a redshift-localized source of reionization $Δτ_{burst}$ in the context of a broad suite of cosmological data to constrain this scenario, finding a preference of approximately $\sim 2-2.5σ$ for a new contribution. Regardless of Planck reprocessing used (PR3 - SRoll2+plik or PR4 - LoLLiPoP+CamSpec/HiLLiPoP), the results are consistent, favoring a new contribution $Δτ_{burst} \sim 0.012$ ($0.001 < Δτ_{burst} < 0.022$ at 95\%) and a similar total optical depth $τ\sim 0.073$. The precise era of reionization is somewhat discrepant depending on the higher-$\ell$ reprocessing used, with HiLLiPoP favoring $z\sim 45$, CamSpec $z\sim 100$ and plik $z\sim 165$. If such a source is present at $40\lesssim z\lesssim150$, LiteBIRD should be able to detect it, while Simons Observatory should also constrain it.

title: Bridging Theory and Observation: Synthetic Far-infrared Insights into Star Formation Efficiency
summary: The star formation efficiency per free-fall time ($ε_{\rm ff}$) quantifies how efficiently giant molecular clouds (GMCs) convert gas into stars and is often observed to be orders of magnitude lower than expected for free-fall collapse. Observers typically estimate $ε_{\rm ff}$ by mapping far-infrared (FIR) dust emission to infer gas surface densities ($Σ_{\rm gas}$) and counting embedded protostars, assuming simplified lifetimes and masses. Using the fiducial STARFORGE radiation-magnetohydrodynamics simulation of an $M_{\rm cl} = 2\times10^4 M_\odot$ GMC that self-consistently models star cluster formation and stellar feedback, we generate synthetic FIR observations and apply the same methodologies used in GMC surveys to investigate this discrepancy. We present the first $ε_{\rm ff}-Σ_{\rm gas}$ analysis in a fully feedback-regulated GMC simulation that resolves the formation of stellar systems. Our synthetic measurements reproduce the low observationally inferred efficiencies, showing that feedback-regulated star formation naturally produces $ε_{\rm ff} \sim 1-3\%$ without requiring extreme initial conditions. We also find that $ε_{\rm ff}$ varies strongly over a GMC's lifetime, suggesting that much of the observed scatter reflects evolutionary sampling rather than intrinsic cloud-to-cloud differences. Finally, by comparing observational and simulation definitions, we show that methodological assumptions introduce systematic biases, with a transition near $\log Σ_{\rm gas} \approx 2.3 M_\odot {\rm pc}^{-2}$ that depends on resolution. Above this threshold, the smoothing of dense structure increases both the inferred free-fall time and enclosed gas, with the latter dominating and suppressing $ε_{\rm ff}$. Below the threshold, the discrepancies are primarily driven by star formation rate assumptions.

title: Exploring Case B I: The Footprints of Hidden Radiation Fields in H I Balmer Decrements
summary: Theory predicts that H I emission from photoionized clouds should lie close to the Case B limit established by Menzel and Baker, and observations of nearby nebulae have largely confirmed this expectation. However, recent observations of more distant high-redshift systems have revealed a small fraction with striking departures from Case B. What additional physics might be at work in these objects? This paper is part of a series exploring the physical processes that can produce such departures. In Paper I (D26), we show that Case B remains remarkably robust over a broad range of physical conditions, consistent with observations of nearby nebulae. Here, we explore one additional ingredient: a soft, non-ionizing radiation field. Such a continuum can strongly perturb the Balmer spectrum. The largest effects occur for radiation fields resembling log(Teff K)\sim 3.2-4.2 blackbodies, where photoexcitation from the metastable 2s level alters the hydrogen level populations and subsequent radiative cascade. The resulting Halpha/Hbeta and Hgamma/Hbeta ratios follow a different trajectory from dust reddening, allowing the two effects to be distinguished using multiple Balmer lines. In unresolved systems, a cool source located near the line-emitting gas may provide an additional radiation field distinct from the hot stars responsible for ionization. Balmer decrements may therefore carry information about otherwise hidden components of the radiation field surrounding the emitting gas.

title: An empirical calibration of the spectral resolution of JWST NIRSpec PRISM
summary: We present an empirical calibration of the effective spectral resolution of the JWST NIRSpec PRISM disperser based on a large sample of galaxies drawn from archival observations. Our sample spans a wide redshift range, $0.5 \lesssim z \lesssim 10$, enabling a wavelength-dependent characterization of the PRISM resolving power across the full bandpass using the [O III]$λ\lambda4959,5007$ doublets. To ensure robust measurements, we impose strict signal-to-noise requirements on both continuum and emission-line detections. Emission-line profiles are fitted with multi-Gaussian models, and the full width at half maximum (FWHM) is measured for each source. The derived empirical resolution curve shows a systematic offset from the nominal pre-launch estimate, lying between the tabulated instrumental resolution and the point-source shutter limit. We also discuss how source size affects the final spectral resolution, and provide an analytical formula that combines wavelength and morphology dependence in a root-sum-square framework. This work delivers a population-averaged, statistically robust calibration of the effective PRISM spectral resolution for typical galaxy observations. The resulting calibration is directly applicable to statistical analyses of galaxy spectra obtained with NIRSpec PRISM. Our empirical calibration exceeds the pre-launch JDox values by a factor of 1.03 to 1.63, depending on source morphology, and provides the first wavelength and morphology dependent calibration of the NIRSpec PRISM spectral resolution.

title: Unifying spherical convolutions through lifting
summary: We develop a unified description of convolution on the sphere by lifting to the rotation group. A number of definitions of spherical convolution have been proposed, differing in whether the kernel is axisymmetric or directional, whether the output is on the sphere or the rotation group, whether the signals carry spin, and in their computational cost. No unified treatment exists. Regarding the sphere as the homogeneous space $S^2 \cong \text{SO(3)}/\text{SO(2)}$, we lift a spin $s$ field to the rotation group, convolve on $\text{SO(3)}$, and project back to the sphere through the adjoint of the lift for a potentially different spin $s'$. We recover every rotation-equivariant convolution considered previously through constraints on the kernel, spin choices and inclusion or omission of the lift and projection. For maps between fields of fixed input and output spin, we prove that directional kernels, output on the sphere and equivariance cannot be achieved simultaneously. We make explicit that spin fields are sections of associated line bundles, linking the physics and bundle literatures, and express the spin rotation phase as the character of the twist of the section. We present harmonic-space algorithms for the exact and efficient computation of lifted spherical convolutions of band-limited fields by appealing to sampling theorems on the sphere and rotation group. All operators are implemented in the open-source s2conv code, and numerical experiments confirm the reductions and the equivariance of the operators to machine precision. Finally, we illustrate the operators on fields measured on the Earth and on the celestial sky.

title: A dust-reddened quasar in a [C II]-luminous host at z=6.55
summary: Most known quasars at $z>6$ were selected through their rest-frame UV emission. Only a small number of reddened quasars have been identified at these redshifts, leaving their nuclear and host-galaxy properties poorly constrained. We present JWST/NIRSpec spectroscopy and ALMA band 6 observations of the quasar J1440+0019 at $z=6.5488$, revealing its dust-reddened nature and jointly characterizing its nucleus and host galaxy. The continuum is best described by an SMC-like extinction law with $E(B-V)=0.20\pm0.03$. Three absorption systems detected in N V, Si IV, and C IV are blueshifted by approximately $900$--$3600$ km s$^{-1}$ and likely trace an ionized nuclear outflow. The broad Mg II line and extinction-corrected continuum yield a black-hole mass of $\log(M_{\rm BH}/M_\odot)=9.04\pm0.42$, a bolometric luminosity of $L_{\rm bol}\simeq1.1\times10^{47}$ erg s$^{-1}$, and an Eddington ratio of $λ_{\rm Edd}\simeq0.8$. ALMA observations further reveal its host galaxy to be among the most [C II]-luminous known at $z>6$, with $L_{\mathrm{[C II]}}=(7.21\pm0.25)\times10^9 L_\odot$. For a fiducial dust temperature of 47 K and emissivity index $β=1.6$, the dust continuum implies $L_{\rm TIR}=8.9\times10^{12} L_\odot$ and $M_{\rm dust}=4.0\times10^8 M_\odot$. The inferred dynamical mass places J1440+0019 in the region of the $M_{\rm BH}$--$M_{\rm dyn}$ plane occupied by high-redshift blue quasars. These observations reveal a moderately reddened, rapidly accreting quasar in a luminous, dust-rich host during reionization. Its measured nuclear and host-galaxy properties provide an observational reference for identifying and characterizing similar systems in future systematic searches with wide-area infrared surveys.

title: A strategy for astrometric quasar selection with Gaia DR3 and its application to discover new luminous $z>2$ quasars
summary: We aim to provide a cookbook for purely astrometric selection of quasars with Gaia DR3 and to provide an example of its use for the identification of very luminous $z>2$ quasars. We analyse the Gaia DR3 astrometry of confirmed quasars and stationary sources. We show that the proper motion signal to noise $μ/σ_μ$ follows a Rayleigh-like distribution. We also show the importance of properly taking into account the correlation between proper motions in right ascension and declination, as well as the non-linear error propagation. We adopt the Mahalanobis distance to the null proper-motion hypothesis. A scaled $χ^2$ distribution with $k=2$ and scale $s=1.1485$ is fitted to Gaia-CRF3; the corresponding $\pm2σ$ Gaussian-equivalent threshold is $D^2_{M(μ)}<7.097$. The final criteria combine this with the parallax condition and $\mathrm{ruwe}<1.4$. Applying the new criteria to the SDSS DR16Q confirmed quasars, the recovery rate is $90.25\%$. The suggested purely astrometric selection significantly improves both completeness and purity compared to other strategies used in the literature, reaching a quasar purity of approximately $95\%$ ($\sim2σ$ Gaussian-equivalent). It can be used to improve the selection purity and completeness for future quasar surveys. As an example, we use the suggested strategi to locate 24 very bright $z>2$ quasars without redshifts in the literature. Our proposed astrometric selection strategy recovers 95\% of known quasars. Its potential use for new discoveries is demonstrated by the identification of 24 very luminous $z>2$ quasars. Ten of these are new discoveries and for an additional seven we correct the redshifts determined by other methods.}

title: High Resolution Spectro-Polarimetric Observations of the Optical Filaments surrounding NGC 1275 with ESPaDOnS
summary: We analyze archival high spectral resolution ESPaDOnS spectropolarimetric observations (R = $λ/Δλ$ = 68000) of three targeted locations within the filamentary nebula surrounding NGC 1275. We present here the analysis of the main filaments emission lines, namely: [NII]$\lambda6584$, H$α$, and [NII]$\lambda6548$, across our three pointings displaying clear detectable emission, with one also showing additional [SII]$\lambda6716$ and [SII]$\lambda6731$ emission line doublet. Using a Markov Chain Monte-Carlo (MCMC) algorithm and thanks to the exceptionally high spectral resolution of the observations, we resolve for the first time each of the emission lines within one of the pointings into a set of three emission components with a remarkable velocity dispersion contrast ($σ_1 \sim 25$ km/s, $σ_2 \sim 90$ km/s and $σ_3 \sim 208$ km/s). We also perform flux ratios of the three detected emission components, which reveal differences in electron density and ionization sources. Consequently, the ESPaDOnS observations appear to reveal for the first time the overlap of an outer quiescent filament and a central turbulent filament likely affected by the AGN activity at a distance of $\sim 6.8''$ ($\sim 2.5$ kpc) from the central BCG. Finally, ESPaDOnS polarimetric data of one of the pointing allows us to confirm an average linear polarization degree of $\sim 0.15-0.14\%$ and an angle of polarization of $5.3\pm25.7^\circ$ for the optical emission of the filaments, as well as polarization dips associated with the H$α$ emission line and its multiple emission components. We interpret these features and measurements as tentative polarization due to dust scattering.

title: First Experimental Results of Space Object Detection Using the InteRFeX Array
summary: This paper presents the first experimental validation of InteRFeX, a non-uniform receive only (passive) array located at the Nova Systems Space Precinct in Peterborough, Australia, designed for space domain awareness applications. It operates over a frequency range of 70 to 300 MHz and is capable of functioning in a range of observational modes, including as a coherent passive bistatic radar for space surveillance, which is the focus of this work. InteRFeX exploits commercial broadcast transmissions as illuminators of opportunity, combining cross-ambiguity function processing for bistatic range and range-rate retrieval with MUSIC-based direction-of-arrival (DoA) estimation for angular localization. The International Space Station (ISS) serves as the experimental target, with measurements evaluated against Two-Line Element (TLE) orbit predictions. Taking advantage of the dual-polarized array, all four reference--surveillance polarization combinations are evaluated, revealing differences in detection rate and mean signal-to-noise ratio (SNR) over the observation pass, with bistatic-range RMSEs of approximately 1 km relative to the TLE-derived reference. Independently, the MUSIC-based DoA estimates exhibit a mean angular separation of approximately $0.45^\circ$ from the TLE-derived reference directions. The angular deviations are further decomposed into along-track and cross-track components, enabling a more detailed characterization of the DoA offsets relative to the TLE-derived reference trajectory. The processing framework also includes a first-order bistatic link-budget analysis to estimate the expected SNR over the observation geometry. These results demonstrate the feasibility of passive-radar space domain awareness using radio-interferometric array technology and establish the proposed signal-processing pipeline as a basis for a dedicated coherent passive-radar mode within InteRFeX.

title: Detecting redshift space distortions with forthcoming 21cm intensity maps from MeerKLASS
summary: Redshift space distortions (RSD) provide a powerful measurement of structure formation in modern cosmology. In this work, we explore the potential of 21cm intensity mapping with the MeerKAT Large Area Synoptic Survey (MeerKLASS) to detect RSD and probe gravity within the redshift range of MeerKAT's UHF band ($0.4<z<1.45$). Using simulated sky observations, we examine the impact from observational effects caused by blind foreground removal and MeerKAT's primary beam, plus $k$-cuts to the measurements. With a multipole expansion formalism, we demonstrate how the quadrupole of the HI power spectrum can be modelled and also show how a foreground transfer function can reconstruct the distorted signal. With 1,115 deg$^2$ of simulated MeerKLASS observations at $0.4<z<1.0$, our proposed analysis pipeline reveals a $6.7σ$ detection of an RSD-induced quadrupole relative to one caused by anisotropic observational effects alone. We also explore parameter inference with the full MeerKLASS 10,000 deg$^2$ survey. Within forecasts, we demonstrate how a tomographic analysis across the full UHF redshift range can be leveraged to address certain parameter degeneracies with e.g. the HI bias ($b_{\rm HI}$) and cosmic density of HI ($Ω_{\rm HI}$). By adopting a redshift-dependent model for the bias and HI density combined with simulation-informed priors, we demonstrate how degeneracies can be alleviated, and indicate the potential for MeerKLASS to reach competitive precision on simple probes of modified gravity.

title: The Silk Nebula: A Newly Discovered Giant [OIII] Emission Filament
summary: We report [O\,\textsc{iii}] narrow-band imaging of an extremely large-scale nebula, the Silk Nebula, discovered by the SWONS (Super Wide-Field [O\,\textsc{iii}] Narrow-band Survey), together with multi-fiber medium-resolution spectroscopic data covering the H$α$, [N\,\textsc{ii}], [S\,\textsc{ii}], and [O\,\textsc{iii}] emission lines, acquired with the Large Sky Area Multi-Object Fiber Spectroscopic Telescope (LAMOST) as part of the Medium-Resolution Spectroscopic Survey of Nebulae (MRS-N). Based on 2,684 high-quality spectra, we measured its physical parameters, including relative line intensities, radial velocities (RVs), and full widths at half-maximum (FWHMs). The [S\,\textsc{ii}]/H$α$ ratio of the nebula significantly exceeds the shock-excitation threshold of 0.4. Its location in BPT diagnostic diagrams and spatial morphology of [O\,\textsc{iii}] both support the optical emission is dominated by shock-heated gas. The oxygen abundance is near solar and spatially uniform, consistent with a shock propagating into the ambient interstellar medium. Because [O\,\textsc{iii}] is the only emission line that clearly traces the nebular morphology, we base our distance estimate exclusively on the [O\,\textsc{iii}] kinematics, obtaining a fiducial distance of $\sim$160 pc. At this distance, the nebula has a physical extent of $\sim$28 pc along the north-south direction. We suggest that the Silk Nebula is a large [O\,\textsc{iii}] filament possibly associated with a supernova remnant, although a diffuse-ionized-gas (DIG) or ionized-bubble origin cannot be ruled out with the present data, and one of the largest angular-scale [O\,\textsc{iii}] emission structures documented to date. Future deep X-ray observations and shock-modeling efforts are required to firmly establish its nature.

title: Predicted state-to-state collisional rate coefficients from neural networks
summary: Molecular spectra observed in the interstellar medium are commonly analyzed using non-local thermodynamic equilibrium models, which requires accurate state-to-state collisional rate coefficients. Close-coupling calculations become prohibitively expensive for transitions from highly excited rotational states, therefore available datasets are often truncated at low initial states and temperatures; and since each new system also requires an accurate ab initio potential energy surface, many detected molecules have no collisional data. We employ two machine learning strategies to predict rotational state-to-state rate coefficients of molecules included in the train set beyond the range of initial states and temperatures computed so far, and predicting those of a molecule absent from training and validation sets. Feed-forward neural networks are trained on state-to-state de-excitation rate coefficients of 24 linear molecules colliding with para-H2. Scheme 1 includes all systems in the train+validation set, with 70%, 80%, and 90% initial-state boundaries and a 90% temperature boundary. Scheme 2 is trained on 22 systems described only by transition and molecular properties, and predicts two excluded systems, CS and CF+, whose astrophysical impact is explored with non-LTE calculations. For the 90% boundary, Scheme 1 predicts 99.4% of the test transitions within a factor of 2, and no prediction deviates from the reference value by more than a factor of 4.7. This model was used to complete 18 datasets. Scheme 2 reproduces the rate coefficients of two excluded systems within a factor of 3 for more than 92% of their transitions. Both schemes provide near-instantaneous complements to close-coupling calculations: Scheme 1 extends the range of a molecule already included in the training set with high accuracy, while Scheme 2 gives a reasonable first estimate for a molecule that has not been studied.

title: "Mega-Earths" are likely an artifact of stellar activity
summary: Empirical relations and planet formation simulations suggest an upper mass limit for rocky planets of $\sim$10M$_{\oplus}$, as cores above this will almost certainly undergo runaway gas accretion. Nevertheless, a small number of planets appear to have densities consistent with rocky Earth-like compositions above this threshold, indicating that unusual formation and evolutionary scenarios are capable of producing extremely massive rocky planets called "Mega-Earths." However, all of these planets orbit active stars with log$R'_{HK}$ $>$-4.75. We find a <1$\%$ probability that all literature ultra-massive rocky planets would coincidentally orbit such active stars, and find no astrophysical reason to expect Mega-Earths to preferentially form around active stars. We therefore conclude that Mega-Earths are artifacts of stellar activity, and we question the reliability of Gaussian Processes to enable mass measurements for rocky planets around active stars.

title: A Single Line-Emitter Identified in an Unbiased Search with JWST/NIRSpec: Multi-Object Coronagraphy for Slitless Spectroscopy
summary: We report the detection of a previously unknown object with a single emission line within the Hubble Ultra Deep Field, using a new JWST NIRSpec technique called Multi-Object Coronagraphy for Slitless Spectroscopy (MOCSS) with the G140M/F100LP observing mode. The MOCSS technique involves opening almost all the shutters on the NIRSpec microshutter array, while simultaneously closing the shutters that lie on top of known low redshift objects, facilitating a wide field slitless spectroscopic search without contamination from bright objects. This observational technique has enabled the detection of a strong emission line in four different dither positions and in two position angles, and thus cannot be artificial. This line is detected at 1.60 $\rm μm$ with a line flux of $[2.5\pm 0.3]\times10^{-18} \rm erg\ s^{-1} cm^{-2}$ and a FWHM of $13.2\pm2.0$Å, and does not correspond to any known source with some of the deepest HST and JWST imaging in existence. Based upon the absence of imaging detection, we place a lower limit on the observed frame equivalent width (EW) of 7620Å on this object, which strongly limits the number of possible lines that this line can be. Given the wavelength, an EW limit that is near the ceiling of expectation, and the lack of other lines in the bandpass, this line cannot be easily explained by [OII] at $z=3.29$, [OIII] at $z=2.20$, H$α$ at $z=1.44$, and Ly$α$ at $z=12.16$. We discuss possible AGN and transient phenomena that could explain the finding.

title: An Ultraviolet Instrument on the Habitable Worlds Observatory: Considerations and Capability Trades on the Multi-Object, Integral-field, and High-resolution modes of a potential UVI
summary: The Habitable Worlds Observatory (HWO) is NASA's next-generation astrophysics platform, delivering transformative capability in the search for life and study of the origins of the universe. Amongst the instruments under consideration for HWO is a multi-purpose ultraviolet spectrograph and imager that provides a deep toolbox for some of the most pressing science investigations of the next several decades. In this paper, we present a basic draft model of a potential UVI, including a multi-object spectrograph, far ultraviolet imager, high resolution spectrograph, and integral-field spectrograph. The draft designs for these channels of the UV instrument serve as a basis for a general discussion of the instrument architecture and design challenges, while also identifying potential trades, enhancements, and other considerations that the HWO project will need to address as it moves into the formulation phase. We conclude with a presentation of several scientific simulations that have helped guide the capabilities of the draft design. This paper is intended to serve as a summary of UV instrument modes, technology, and potential design ahead of planned instrument studies in the late 2020's, and then Phase A in the early 2030's.

title: Assessing PLATO's Discovery Potential across Different Observing Strategies
summary: The PLATO mission, planned to launch in spring 2027, will observe a fixed Southern field, LOPS2, for at least 2 years with the goal of discovering and deriving precise parameters for planets as small as Earth around FGK dwarfs and sub-giants. Afterwards, PLATO could continue to monitor the same field or move to a Northern field, LOPN1, overlapping with the Kepler field. We assess these two observing strategies in terms of sensitivity of detecting small and long period planets, and subsequently we estimate yields for both observing strategies. Within this we account for including the Kepler data in the LOPN1 field, monitoring of up to 8 years of the LOPS2 field, and the sensitivity improvement from combining TESS and PLATO data since both fields have been and will be continued to be observed with TESS. We find that by monitoring both fields, and hence more stars, the total number of newly discovered planets is maximised. However, to optimise the number of discovered small and long periods planets, long-term monitoring of one field produces the best results. The combination of Kepler and PLATO data improves detection sensitivities; however, as this only covers a fraction of the LOPN1 field and stellar sample, it improves the yields of small and long period planets only marginally. Hence, to detect and characterise small and long period planets in this sparsely explored exoplanet parameter space, a longer continuous observation of the LOPS2 field is best.

title: General Spin-1 Dynamics During Inflation: Microcausality Constraints and Cosmological Collider Signals
summary: We construct the general theory of a spin-1 field propagating on an inflationary background consistent with scale invariance, rotations, Bunch-Davies conditions and microcausality. Our Boostless Proca theory generalises the usual massive Proca theory to a Lagrangian with 5 free parameters: 4 corresponding to parity-even terms and a single parity-odd term. We impose three degrees of freedom from the outset and find that microcausality, the statement that field operators vanish outside the lightcone, requires the kinetic terms to be gauge invariant. We couple this spin-1 state to the inflaton and study the signatures it imprints on cosmological correlators. We find no new signals for the bispectrum meaning that the known signals are the most general thereby providing a very clean model-independent probe of new physics in this leading form of non-Gaussianity. For the trispectrum and higher-point functions, the boostless Proca theory produces new shapes with all 5 parameters in principle measurable.

title: A Comprehensive JWST Slitless Spectroscopic Census of $\sim$12,000 Emission-Line Galaxies at Redshift $0\sim9$ in COSMOS
summary: Emission-line galaxies provide key diagnostics of star formation, chemical enrichment, and AGN activity across cosmic time. We present a systematic census of emission-line sources using JWST/NIRCam wide-field slitless spectroscopy (WFSS) from the COSMOS-3D program, which covers a large contiguous area of 0.33 deg$^2$ and provides F444W grism spectroscopy over $3.9$--$5.1\ μ$m. By combining slitless spectroscopy with deep multi-band imaging data, we construct a homogeneous spectroscopic sample of 12,275 objects at redshift 0--9. The typical $3σ$ line-flux limit reaches $3.2\times10^{-18}\ {\rm erg\ s^{-1}\ cm^{-2}}$. To address source confusion inherent to slitless spectroscopy, we develop a multi-step identification framework that combines information from spectra, images, spectral energy distributions, and spatial distributions. We introduce convolutional neural network and large language model to emulate the human identification process and improve efficiency. The resulting catalog provides spectroscopic redshifts, emission-line measurements, and derived physical properties for all sources. The F444W WFSS enables the detection of multiple emission lines, including primarily [O III], H$α$, He I $\lambda10830$, [S III] $λ\lambda9531,9069$, Pa$β$, Pa$α$, Br$β$, PAH, Br$α$, allowing a continuous census of galaxies across cosmic time. We construct composite spectra in several redshift bins and detect a variety of faint spectral features that are difficult to identify in individual spectra, including higher-order hydrogen recombination lines, CO absorption bands, and [Fe II] lines. This catalog provides a key reference dataset for studies of galaxy evolution and AGN activity, and demonstrates the power of WFSS for constructing large, unbiased spectroscopic samples over wide areas. The full catalog will be publicly available online upon publication.

title: Insights from the stability of methanol maser flare properties I: G9.62+0.20E
summary: The brightest 6.7 GHz methanol maser in the Galaxy is associated with the high-mass star-forming region (HMSFR) G009.62+0.20E. Additionally, this methanol maser shows periodic flaring observed at 6.7 and 12.2 GHz. Several models have been hypothesized to explain the periodicity, including periodic accretion, spiral shocks in the gaps of circumbinary disks, pulsating stars, dicke's superradiance, and a colliding wind binary (CWB) system. We analyzed the time series of the 1.22 km s-1 feature of the 6.7 GHz methanol maser spectrum and the 1.25 km s-1 feature of the 12.2 GHz methanol maser spectrum over the monitoring duration of roughly 20 years, to determine an updated period, analyze the stability and repeatability of the flares, the temporal behavior of the flare profile, and the duty cycle of the flare profile based on the updated period. From these results, it is argued for or against any of the mechanisms that have been proposed to explain the periodicity. Lomb-Scargle (LS) and phase dispersion minimization (PDM) methods were used to determine the methanol maser period at 6.7 and 12.2 GHz. Once the period has been determined, phase-folding or period-folding was used to analyze the flare shape, flare stability, and duty cycle of the flares. The periods of the 6.7 and 12.2 GHz methanol masers were determined to be ~ 243.0 +- 0.3 days. The flares are highly repeatable, stable, and show almost identical shapes, as well as their duty cycles. A replicated kernel density estimator (KDE) of the flare shape reproduces the time series very well over a time span of ~ 8000 days. After careful consideration of the proposed mechanisms for periodic methanol masers, we conclude that all but one, the CWB model, have been ruled out as a possible driver of this flare profile. It has also been established that the CWB model can qualitatively explain the flare profile of the periodic methanol masers.

title: Relaxation Dark Energy: Compositional Dynamics and the Future of Cosmic Acceleration
summary: If cosmic acceleration is driven by a positive cosmological constant, the universe approaches an eternally accelerating de Sitter state, whose interpretation in quantum gravity remains elusive. We develop a framework in which acceleration is instead a transient stage of dark-sector relaxation towards compositional equilibrium: matter and dark energy approach a stationary density ratio, eventually diluting like pressureless matter. Guided by linear response theory and Onsager's near-equilibrium regression hypothesis, we describe this evolution through a composition variable measuring departure from equilibrium. Extending constant fractional relaxation to the full background evolution yields the dark-energy equation of state $w=w_0a^{-n}$, where $n$ is the relaxation rate per e-fold of expansion. This history connects early dark-energy suppression, an upward phantom crossing and a density maximum to a pressureless scaling future. Using DESI DR2 BAO and Planck distance priors, with and without three alternative supernova compilations, we find a nominal $2.6$--$3.6σ$ preference for nonzero relaxation over constant $w$. The composition framework also motivates a constitutive prescription for linear perturbations that remains regular at phantom crossing. Near equilibrium, regular long-wavelength composition disturbances relax at the background rate to leading order, while small-scale fluctuations propagate as damped sound waves. We prove, however, that for separately conserved matter and dark energy, the pointwise constitutive relation cannot sustain a regular, gradient-stable negative-pressure branch throughout its full past evolution. We explore modifications of the pressure response and their consistency with neighbouring homogeneous histories, identifying requirements for extending the near-equilibrium description to the full cosmological evolution.

title: The Redshift-Space Galaxy Power Spectrum at Two-Loop Order
summary: Contemporary large-scale structure analyses center around the galaxy power spectrum, modeled with one-loop perturbation theory. This description naturally breaks down at large wavenumbers, prohibiting the extraction of cosmological information from small-scale clustering. In this work, we present a complete model for the redshift-space galaxy power spectrum up to two-loop order, derived in the framework of the Effective Field Theory of Large Scale Structure. This accounts for a wide variety of effects, including fifth-order galaxy bias, redshift-space distortions, small-scale non-linearities, spatial non-locality, long-wavelength bulk flows, coordinate distortions, and stochasticity, involving a total of 49 free coefficients. Our model additionally encodes all deterministic contributions to the one-loop bispectrum and trispectrum (as well as the tree-level quadspectrum and pentaspectrum), which depend on many of the same parameters. We implement the model numerically, using the \textsc{vegas} algorithm to precompute the loop integrals; this allows the full likelihood to be evaluated in milliseconds. The approach is validated using power spectra measured from high-resolution simulations, considering both dark matter and realistic galaxy samples. The extension to two-loop order greatly increases the range of scales over which the power spectrum can be modeled, with $k_{\rm max}$ rising from $0.2h\,\mathrm{Mpc}^{-1}$ to $0.34h\,\mathrm{Mpc}^{-1}$ for a luminous red galaxy sample at $z=0.5$. Much of the additional information is absorbed by the numerous fifth-order biases and counterterms; for this reason, constraints on $σ_8$ are not significantly enhanced by the inclusion of two-loop terms. Future work will assess the full implications of the two-loop model for cosmological parameter inference, both alone and in combination with higher-order statistics.

title: Turbulence modes in molecular clouds in M33: a challenging test of the Brunt-Federrath framework
summary: Understanding the turbulent structure of molecular clouds is essential for linking galactic environment to the regulation of star formation. Although Galactic molecular clouds have been studied extensively, extending turbulence-mode analysis beyond the Milky Way remains challenging because of the limited spatial resolution and dynamic range of extragalactic observations. We assess the applicability of the Brunt \& Federrath (2014; BF14) framework to molecular clouds in M33. We apply BF14 to 128 $^{13}$CO(2-1) clouds, selecting a primary quality-controlled sample of 54 clouds and a more restrictive 25-cloud subsample defined using a stricter extraction-padding criterion (PAD=2) for quantitative analysis.Tests of cloud and noise power spectra, Fourier-space cutoffs, extraction padding, and Monte Carlo uncertainties demonstrate that the retained spatial frequencies are dominated by astrophysical signal and that the inferred turbulence-mode fractions are robust against reasonable analysis choices. Both samples yield consistent distributions of the solenoidal fraction, with mean values of $R \simeq 0.22$ for both samples and median values of $R \simeq 0.18$ and $0.17$, respectively, indicating that compressive motions dominate the turbulent energy budget. No strong systematic variations of $R$ are found with galactocentric distance or tracers of recent star formation. These results demonstrate that, despite the challenging spatial resolution of current extragalactic molecular-line observations, the BF14 framework can be applied reliably to nearby galaxies using spectroscopic observations alone. To our knowledge, this constitutes the first application of the full BF14 formalism to extragalactic molecular-cloud observations.

title: Galaxy Clustering Can Reveal Host-Galaxy Properties of Binary Black Hole Mergers
summary: Galaxy clustering encodes information about the host galaxies of binary black hole (BBH) mergers even when individual hosts remain unidentified, because the distribution of neighboring galaxies depends statistically on the host-galaxy population. We construct event-level host-type likelihoods from host-conditioned galaxy-count distributions within gravitational-wave localization regions and combine them to infer the fractions of BBH mergers hosted by different galaxy populations. The framework applies to common and rare galaxy populations without prescribing formation efficiencies or merger delay-time distributions. Using measured star-forming and quenched galaxy clustering, idealized one-year forecasts assuming all mergers occur in quenched galaxies yield median one-sided 90% lower credible limits of 0.19, 0.48, and 0.92 on the quenched-host fraction for O5, post-O5, and third-generation networks. These forecasts illustrate the potential for host-galaxy population inference before the third-generation detector era.

title: Nailing down the Hubble constant value through time delay cosmography: A 3% measurement from SN Refsdal
summary: We present the first inference of the Hubble constant and matter density parameter from a strongly lensed supernova (SN) by exploiting the mass model of a galaxy cluster enhanced by an extended surface brightness reconstruction. This has resulted in the most precise H0 measurement from a single strong lens so far, outperforming the 3.9% result from the lensed quasar DES J048-5354. Building upon the mass model of MACS J1149.5+2223 relying on image positions only, we incorporate the surface brightness distribution of the SN Refsdal host, to infer some cosmological parameter values within a flat LCDM framework. We consider two cosmological parameterizations, with either H0 and $Ω_m$ or H0 alone treated as free parameters. We explore four different mass-model realizations to assess some of the systematic uncertainties associated with the constraint weighting and source reconstruction. Although known as one of the main systematic effects, we deliberately keep the cluster total mass parametrization fixed to that of the previously published point-like mass model to enable a fair comparison. This reveals that incorporating 77,000 HST pixels reduces the uncertainty on the inferred value of H0 by a factor of 2.0. Our final measurements are $H_0=65.0^{+2.0}_{-1.8}$ km/s/Mpc and $Ω_m=0.30^{+0.08}_{-0.09}$, in agreement with previous results from lensed SNe. This corresponds to a substantially improved precision, reaching a remarkable 3.0% uncertainty on the value of H0. The contributions of the uncertainties on the lens total mass and on the measured time delays to the final H0 error are now comparable, indicating that future improvements will depend on more precise time-delay measurements and continued control of systematic effects. With sub-percent time-delay values reachable at cluster-scale, this mass model approach has the power to lead to unprecedentedly precise H0 measurements.
